comprehension_retry.en: Thank you for putting that in your own words. I'm not sure yet that I explained it clearly enough. Could you tell me in a sentence what you understood from my last explanation, or tell me which part you would like me to go over again?

note: Approved templates. Figures are bound BY REFERENCE ({{value:<value_id>}}) from get_member_values results (B2). The model may choose wording around a template but never writes a figure itself. An approved answer-goal template takes precedence for that task and language without changing the selected strategy. Otherwise the runtime picks the first variant whose placeholders are all present in the member's official values.

text.en: I'm happy to help you understand your letter. We can take it one step at a time. I don't have your letter here. Please share the sentence or section you'd like explained, leaving out personal details. Which part would you like help with?
text.nl: Ik help je graag om je brief te begrijpen. We kunnen dit stap voor stap bekijken. Ik heb je brief hier niet. Deel de zin of het onderdeel dat je wilt laten uitleggen, zonder persoonsgegevens. Welk deel wil je bespreken?

T-S1.pensioner: In short: the Wtp transition (invaren) changes how your pension is organised, not the official amounts you have built up. Your current official monthly pension is {{value:current_monthly_pension}}. The fund's administrator calculated your figures; I can only explain them.
T-S1.active_member: In short: the Wtp transition (invaren) converts the pension you have built up into the new contract; it does not take entitlements away. Under the old contract you had built up {{value:accrued_annual_pension}}. The administrator's official conversion shows a personal pension capital of {{value:personal_capital_after_transition}}. I can only explain these figures, not change them.

T-S2.pensioner: Here is a worked example with your own official figures. Today you receive {{value:current_monthly_pension}} a month. The administrator's transition calculation shows {{value:monthly_pension_after_transition}} a month directly after the transition, as of {{asof:monthly_pension_after_transition}}. After the transition your pension can move with the fund's results each year.
T-S2.active_member: Here is a worked example with your own official figures. Under the old contract you had built up {{value:accrued_annual_pension}}. On {{value:transition_date}} the administrator converts this into a personal pension capital of {{value:personal_capital_after_transition}}, as of {{asof:personal_capital_after_transition}}. From then on that capital moves with the fund's results.

T-S3.pensioner: Think of it as a timeline. Before the transition: your pension is {{value:current_monthly_pension}} a month. On the transition date: your entitlements are converted. Directly after: the official calculation shows {{value:monthly_pension_after_transition}} a month. After that: yearly adjustments depend on the fund's results.
T-S3.active_member: Think of it as a timeline. Before the transition: you have built up {{value:accrued_annual_pension}}. On {{value:transition_date}}: your entitlements are converted. Directly after: the official calculation shows a personal pension capital of {{value:personal_capital_after_transition}}. After that: it moves with contributions and the fund's results.

T-S4.pensioner: What stays the same: your official monthly pension directly after the transition is {{value:monthly_pension_after_transition}}, and it is paid on the same date. What changes: from then on, the yearly adjustment depends on the fund's results. What to check: the transition letter dated {{asof:monthly_pension_after_transition}}.
T-S4.active_member: What stays the same: what you have built up is converted, not lost, and the fund still pays your pension. What changes: from {{value:transition_date}} your pension is shown as a personal pension capital - officially {{value:personal_capital_after_transition}}. What to check: the figures in your transition letter.

T-S5.pensioner: Let me take this step by step. Step 1: today you receive {{value:current_monthly_pension}} a month. Step 2: the administrator's official calculation for directly after the transition is {{value:monthly_pension_after_transition}} a month. Step 3: after that, the yearly adjustment can go up or down with the fund's results. To check I explained this clearly: in your own words, what happens to your monthly pension on the transition date?
T-S5.active_member: Let me take this step by step. Step 1: under the old contract you had built up {{value:accrued_annual_pension}}. Step 2: on {{value:transition_date}} the administrator converts this into a personal pension capital of {{value:personal_capital_after_transition}}. Step 3: after that, the capital moves with contributions and the fund's results. To check I explained this clearly: in your own words, what happens to what you have built up on the transition date?

T-S6.any: If you would like to talk this through with a person, I can arrange a call with one of the fund's advisors. Would that help?
